name: Dal Tadka
steps: Boil toor dal with turmeric and salt until soft.
Prepare a tadka of cumin, garlic and dry chillies in a little oil.
Pour the tadka over the dal and simmer for 2 minutes.
notes: Classic everyday dal. For vegan, temper in oil instead of ghee.

name: Palak Paneer
steps: Blanch and purée the spinach.
Sauté onion, ginger-garlic and spices, add the spinach purée.
Fold in paneer cubes and simmer for 5 minutes.

name: Rajma Chawal
steps: Cook the rajma in an onion-tomato masala until thick.
Serve hot over steamed rice.

name: Chana Masala
steps: Simmer boiled chickpeas and potato in a spiced onion-tomato gravy.
Finish with garam masala and fresh coriander.

name: Soya Chunk Curry
steps: Boil soya chunks, squeeze out water.
Cook in an onion-tomato masala with potato until the gravy thickens.
notes: High-protein vegetarian/vegan main.

name: Paneer Bhurji
steps: Crumble paneer.
Sauté onion, tomato, green chilli and spices, then toss in the paneer.

name: Sprouts Chaat Salad
steps: Toss sprouts with chopped onion, tomato and cucumber.
Season with lemon juice, chaat masala and salt.

name: Oats Banana Porridge
steps: Cook oats in milk until creamy.
Top with sliced banana and chopped almonds.
notes: Swap milk for a plant milk to make it vegan.

name: Tofu & Spinach Stir-fry
steps: Pan-sear cubed tofu until golden.
Add spinach and a splash of soy sauce; toss for a minute.

name: Egg Bhurji
steps: Scramble eggs with onion, tomato, green chilli and spices.

name: Grilled Chicken Rice Bowl
steps: Grill the seasoned chicken breast and slice.
Serve over brown rice with sautéed spinach.
notes: High-protein, balanced bowl.

references.title: Grilled Chicken Rice Bowl nutrient basis

name: Khajur Anjeer Ladoo (no added sugar)
steps: Deseed the dates and soak the figs in warm water for 10 minutes, then chop both fine.
Dry-roast the cashews, almonds and walnuts on low heat until fragrant, cool and coarsely crush.
Blend the dates and figs to a sticky paste.
Warm the paste in a pan for 4-5 minutes until it leaves the sides, then fold in the crushed nuts.
Cool slightly and roll into 12 ladoos. Keeps for a week in an airtight jar.
notes: No added sugar - all sweetness is from the dates and figs. One ladoo is roughly 35 g.

references.title: Dates and figs ladoo without sugar

name: Rava Sheera
steps: Roast the rava in ghee on low heat until it smells nutty and turns pale golden, about 8 minutes.
Fry the cashews and raisins in the same ghee and set aside.
Bring 300 ml water to a boil with the sugar, stirring until dissolved.
Pour the hot syrup into the roasted rava slowly, stirring hard to avoid lumps.
Cover and cook 3-4 minutes until the sheera leaves the sides of the pan; fold in the nuts.
notes: Ghee-heavy by design - reduce the ghee to 20 g to cut roughly 70 kcal per 100 g.

name: Rava Upma
steps: Dry-roast the rava until fragrant and set aside.
Heat the oil, splutter the mustard seeds, then add curry leaves, green chilli and onion; saute until the onion is soft.
Add 300 ml water and the salt, and bring to a rolling boil.
Lower the heat and pour in the rava in a steady stream, stirring continuously.
Cover and steam 3-4 minutes until the water is absorbed and the upma is fluffy.
notes: Vegan as written. A tablespoon of ghee instead of oil makes it vegetarian but not vegan.

name: Idli
steps: Soak the rice and urad dal separately for 5-6 hours.
Grind the urad dal to a light, airy paste and the rice to a slightly coarse one; combine with the salt.
Ferment the batter 8-12 hours in a warm place until it has visibly risen.
Pour into greased idli moulds and steam 10-12 minutes until a skewer comes out clean.
notes: Fermentation raises B-vitamin availability. Batter absorbs water, so cooked yield is far above raw ingredient weight.

name: Medu Vada
steps: Soak the urad dal 4 hours, drain well and grind to a thick fluffy batter using as little water as possible.
Beat in the chopped chilli, ginger, curry leaves and salt.
Wet your palm, shape a portion into a disc and make a hole in the centre.
Deep-fry on medium heat until golden and crisp on both sides; drain on paper.
notes: The 25 g oil is absorbed oil, not the frying quantity. Deep-frying drives off water, so the yield is well below the raw batter weight.

name: Dosa (plain)
steps: Soak the rice and urad dal separately for 5-6 hours, then grind to a smooth batter and add salt.
Ferment 8-12 hours until risen and slightly sour; thin with water to a pouring consistency.
Heat a tawa, pour a ladle of batter and spread outward in a spiral to a thin circle.
Drizzle oil around the edge and cook until the base is golden and the dosa lifts off cleanly.
notes: Plain sada dosa with no potato filling. A masala dosa adds roughly the aloo sabji panel on top.

name: Seviyan Kheer (sweet shevaya)
steps: Fry the cashews and raisins in ghee until golden and set aside.
Roast the vermicelli in the same ghee until it turns light brown.
Bring the milk to a boil, add the roasted vermicelli and simmer until soft, stirring often.
Stir in the sugar and simmer 5 more minutes until it thickens slightly; top with the fried nuts.
notes: The milk reduces while simmering, so the cooked yield is below the sum of the raw ingredients.

name: Semiya Upma (spicy shevaya)
steps: Dry-roast the vermicelli until golden and set aside.
Heat the oil, splutter the mustard seeds, then add curry leaves, chilli and onion and saute until soft.
Pour in 250 ml water with the salt and bring to a boil.
Add the roasted vermicelli, cover and cook on low until the water is absorbed and the strands are separate.
notes: The savoury counterpart to seviyan kheer - same vermicelli, no milk or sugar.

name: Masoor Dal Tadka
steps: Pressure-cook the masoor dal with turmeric and salt until soft.
Heat the oil, crackle the cumin, then fry the garlic and onion until golden.
Add the tomato and cook until it breaks down and the oil separates.
Pour the tadka over the dal, simmer 5 minutes and adjust the consistency with hot water.
notes: Vegan as written; a spoon of ghee in the tadka is the common non-vegan variation.

name: Moong Dal Khichdi (plain)
steps: Rinse equal parts rice and moong dal and pressure-cook with turmeric, salt and plenty of water until very soft.
Mash lightly to a soft, porridge-like consistency and stir in the ghee.
notes: The plain, easily digestible version served when unwell. See khichdi-tadka for the spiced one.

name: Masala Khichdi (tadka)
steps: Pressure-cook the rice and moong dal with turmeric and salt until soft.
Heat the ghee and oil, crackle the cumin, then saute the onion, green chilli and tomato until the oil separates.
Fold the tadka through the cooked khichdi and simmer 2 minutes.
notes: Swap the ghee for oil to make this vegan.

name: Aloo Sabji
steps: Heat the oil and crackle the cumin seeds.
Saute the onion until golden, then add the tomato, turmeric, coriander and chilli powder and cook until the oil separates.
Add the cubed boiled potato and salt, toss to coat and cook 5 minutes.
Add a splash of water for a looser gravy and finish with coriander leaves.
notes: Dry Punjabi-style aloo. Add 150 ml water for the thinner rassa version.

name: Cabbage Sabji
steps: Heat the oil and splutter the mustard seeds.
Add the green chilli and turmeric, then the shredded cabbage and salt.
Cover and cook on medium heat 8-10 minutes, stirring once, until the cabbage wilts but keeps a bite.
Finish with the grated coconut.
notes: Cabbage loses a lot of water, so the cooked yield is well under the raw weight.

name: Cauliflower Sabji
steps: Heat the oil and saute the onion until translucent.
Add the tomato and the ground spices and cook until the oil separates.
Add the cauliflower florets, potato cubes and salt; toss to coat.
Cover and cook on low 12-15 minutes, stirring gently, until the cauliflower is tender.
notes: The classic aloo-gobi ratio. Leave out the potato for a lighter side.

name: Tomato Sabji
steps: Heat the oil and crackle the cumin seeds.
Saute the onion briefly, then add the chopped tomato, turmeric, chilli powder and salt.
Cook covered on low 10 minutes until the tomato collapses into a thick pulp.
Stir in the jaggery to balance the acidity and simmer 2 more minutes.
notes: The jaggery is what stops this tasting sharp - do not skip it.

name: Methi Sabji
steps: Wash the methi leaves well, chop and squeeze out the excess water to reduce bitterness.
Heat the oil, fry the crushed garlic and green chilli, then add the turmeric.
Add the methi and potato cubes with the salt.
Cook uncovered on medium heat 8 minutes so the leaves lose their raw water.
notes: A strong source of calcium and vitamin K. Squeezing the leaves cuts the bitterness.

name: Bhindi Sabji
steps: Wash and dry the okra completely, then cut into rounds - any water makes it slimy.
Heat the oil and fry the okra uncovered on medium-high heat 10 minutes without stirring too often.
Add the onion and cook until the sliminess is gone and the edges crisp.
Stir in the ground spices and salt and cook 2 more minutes.
notes: Never cover the pan - trapped steam is what makes bhindi slimy.

name: Bhopla Sabji (pumpkin)
steps: Heat the oil and splutter the mustard seeds.
Add the turmeric and the cubed pumpkin with the salt and toss to coat.
Cover and cook on low 12 minutes until the pumpkin is soft enough to mash against the pan.
Stir in the jaggery and chilli powder and cook 2 more minutes - it should taste sweet-sour-hot.
notes: Very high in vitamin A. The jaggery is traditional, not optional, in the Maharashtrian version.

name: Kanda Poha
steps: Rinse the poha in a colander until just softened, then drain and rest 10 minutes - never soak it.
Heat the oil, splutter the mustard seeds, fry the peanuts, then add curry leaves, chilli and onion.
Saute until the onion is translucent, add the turmeric and salt.
Fold in the poha gently, cover and steam 3 minutes. Finish with lemon and coriander.
notes: Rinse, never soak - soaked poha turns to paste.

name: Aloo Paratha
steps: Knead the atta with water and a little salt into a soft dough and rest it 20 minutes.
Mash the boiled potato with onion, chilli, coriander, chilli powder and salt.
Stuff a portion of filling into a dough ball, seal and roll out gently to an even disc.
Cook on a hot tawa, smearing ghee on both sides, until golden brown spots appear.
notes: Roll gently and evenly - pressing hard tears the seal and the filling escapes.

name: Methi Thepla
steps: Mix the atta, besan, chopped methi, turmeric, chilli powder and salt.
Add the curd and a little oil and knead to a soft, pliable dough; rest 15 minutes.
Roll thin discs and roast on a tawa with a little oil until brown spots appear on both sides.
Cool completely before stacking - they keep for 2-3 days of travel.
notes: Made with curd, so vegetarian rather than vegan. Travels well without refrigeration.

name: Khaman Dhokla
steps: Whisk the besan with water, ginger-chilli paste, sugar and salt into a smooth lump-free batter.
Stir in the eno or soda right before steaming and pour immediately into a greased tray.
Steam 15-18 minutes until a skewer comes out clean, then cool and cut into squares.
Pour over a tempering of mustard seeds and curry leaves in hot oil with a little sugar water.
notes: Add the raising agent last and steam at once, or the batter loses its lift.

name: Sambar
steps: Pressure-cook the toor dal with turmeric until completely soft and whisk smooth.
Boil the mixed vegetables with tamarind extract until just tender.
Add the cooked dal, sambar powder and salt and simmer 8-10 minutes.
Finish with a tempering of mustard seeds and curry leaves in hot oil.
notes: Any firm vegetable works - drumstick, brinjal and ash gourd are all traditional.

name: Rasam
steps: Extract the tamarind in 500 ml warm water and discard the solids.
Simmer the tamarind water with crushed tomato, turmeric, rasam powder and salt until the raw smell goes.
Add the thin cooked dal and heat through - do not let it boil hard once the dal is in.
Temper mustard, cumin, garlic and curry leaves in oil and pour over; finish with coriander.
notes: Thin and drinkable by design. Never boil after adding the dal or it goes cloudy.

name: Curd Rice
steps: Mash the warm cooked rice lightly so it loses its grain structure.
Cool to room temperature, then mix in the curd and milk with salt - never add curd to hot rice.
Temper mustard seeds, curry leaves, chilli and ginger in oil and stir through.
Rest 20 minutes before serving so the flavours settle.
notes: Cool the rice first - hot rice splits the curd and turns it sour.

name: Pav Bhaji
steps: Boil and mash the potato, cauliflower and peas together into a coarse pulp.
Fry the onion in ghee until golden, add the tomato and cook until the fat separates.
Add the chilli powder and pav bhaji masala, then the mashed vegetables and salt; mash further in the pan.
Simmer 10 minutes with a little water until thick, and toast the split pav in ghee until crisp.
notes: The ghee is what makes it taste like the street version. The pav is counted in the yield.

name: Chole (chana masala)
steps: Fry the onion in oil until deep golden, then add the ginger-garlic paste.
Add the tomato and ground spices and cook until the oil separates cleanly.
Add the boiled chana with some of its cooking water and the salt.
Simmer 15 minutes, mashing a few chickpeas to thicken the gravy.
notes: Mashing a spoonful of the chana is what thickens the gravy without cream.

name: Vegetable Pulao
steps: Heat the ghee, crackle the cumin and fry the cashews until golden.
Saute the sliced onion until light brown, then add the carrot and peas.
Add the garam masala and salt and toss for a minute.
Fold in the cooked rice gently so the grains stay separate, and steam covered 3 minutes.
notes: Fold, do not stir - stirring breaks the grains and turns pulao into khichdi.

name: Jowar Bhakri
steps: Mix the jowar flour with salt and hot water and knead to a firm, smooth dough.
Pat a ball out by hand into a round disc, dusting with dry flour - a rolling pin cracks it.
Roast on a hot tawa, wet the top surface with water, flip and cook until it puffs.
Finish directly over the flame for a few seconds until it balloons.
notes: Gluten-free and hand-patted. Hot water in the dough is what holds it together.

name: Puri
steps: Knead the atta with salt and just enough water into a stiff dough - stiffer than roti dough.
Rest 15 minutes, then roll into small even discs without any dusting flour.
Slide into hot oil and press down gently with a slotted spoon so it puffs up.
Flip once, fry until pale gold and drain well.
notes: The 35 g oil is absorbed oil, not the frying quantity. Stiff dough and hot oil are what make puris puff.

name: Ven Pongal
steps: Dry-roast the moong dal until fragrant, then pressure-cook it with the rice until very soft.
Mash lightly to a soft, porridge-like texture.
Fry the cashews, cumin, crushed pepper, ginger and curry leaves in ghee.
Pour the tempering over and mix well with the salt.
notes: The savoury breakfast pongal, distinct from the sweet sakkarai pongal.

name: Misal
steps: Cook the sprouts with turmeric and salt until just tender but not mushy.
Fry the onion and coconut in oil until dark golden, then grind to a kala masala paste with the spices.
Add the tomato and paste to the sprouts with water and simmer into a thin spicy usal.
Serve topped with farsan, raw onion and coriander, with pav on the side.
notes: The tarri (spicy oil layer) on top is the point. Pav is served alongside and not counted in this yield.
